errors.description: The final exponential-divisibility characterization is false without restricting d to primes occurring initially. For any absent prime q, every positive exponent v_q(d) divides all zero initial valuations, so arbitrary powers of q may be adjoined and no maximal d exists. This does not affect the proof.
errors.quote: the unique maximal $d$ with $v_p(d) \mid v_p(a_i)$ for all $p$ and all $i$.

parsed.notes: The termination argument and prime-wise invariant give a complete, rigorous solution. Only the optional final remark needs a support restriction.
